Evidence:
Host has llvmpipe (/usr/share/vulkan/icd.d/lvp_icd.x86_64.json, mesa-vulkan-drivers 23.2.1) next to nvidia_icd.json. Recorded hangs were NVIDIA driver threads (AGENTS.md:162-163). 3. Set VK_ICD_FILENAMES in `just test` too (only when the lvp ICD file exists, so CI is unaffected).
4. Replace the CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md deadlock warnings with 'use `just test-gpu`'; fix the wrong crate name; document PROTOC.

hud-bstmy.1.6.title: Reconcile spec-to-code (gen-1) for T8.0: Enablers (GPU recipe, CI parity, test-file splits)
hud-bstmy.1.6.description:
Deep-dive review: compare the original spec/requirements (see epic description and docs/scope.md T8 row, docs/invariants.md) against the implementation delivered by sibling beads under this epic.

Mindset: audit the CODEBASE against the spec, not the sibling diffs against their bead descriptions. Your job is to FALSIFY the coverage claim, not to collect confirming evidence. A requirement counts as implemented only after you have read the implementing code; a test existing or the suite being green is never sufficient evidence by itself.

Workflow:
1. Re-read the epic description and all sibling bead descriptions/acceptance criteria.
2. Audit the code. Start from the sibling diffs, but treat the whole codebase as in scope; spec invariants bind pre-existing code too.
3. For every universal or negative requirement ("no X anywhere", "every Y must", "the only path is Z"): enumerate ALL code paths performing that operation (search the repo) and verify each one.
4. Audit the instruments: for every guardrail/scan test, read its regex, glob and scan roots and check they cover the mandated surface. For every spec scenario confirm ONE gate pins it (a behavior-executing test, or the designated scan guard for structural invariants).
5. Where several surfaces implement the same contract, diff them against each other (filters, defaults, ordering, authz).
6. Produce a checklist mapping every requirement to its implementing bead and code evidence (file:line), classified implemented/partial/missing/deviates.
7. For every partial or missing requirement, report a cold-start-ready gap candidate in Discovered-Follow-Ups-JSON (priority, parent, deps, exact spec link, acceptance evidence, gate species, expected net test delta).
8. When gaps remain, report the need for a gen-2 reconciliation and return blocked-awaiting-coordinator with "coverage gaps remain" as the unblock condition.
9. The coordinator dedupes/materializes gaps and closes lifecycle state; this worker never mutates Beads lifecycle.
hud-bstmy.1.6.design: Spec sources: docs/scope.md T8 row and Working rules, docs/invariants.md (every named test exists), docs/vision.md, plus every sibling bead under hud-bstmy.1 (their Files/Evidence lists define the deletion surface; verify each deletion grep is empty and each kept test exists). Runs last among implementation siblings. Escalation (needs-human) siblings are deliberately NOT dependencies: their default is status quo, so reconciliation must not wait on an owner answer; if one was answered, include its follow-up bead.
hud-bstmy.1.6.acceptance_criteria:
1. Every requirement in the epic spec has a corresponding implementation bead.
2. Universal/negative invariants are verified by enumerating every code path that performs the operation, not by citing a single compliant example.
3. Guardrail/scan tests were audited for blind spots, and every spec scenario is pinned by exactly one gate species; no gap candidate proposes tests for a scenario that already has one.
4. Any gaps found are reported as dedupe-ready child-bead candidates under the same epic.
5. If gaps were found, the handoff reports a next-generation reconciliation candidate.
6. The close reason records the reconciliation summary.

A shared lock or serialization in HeadlessRuntime::new would close it for hosts running cargo test directly with a hardware ICD.
hud-bstmy.1.12.design:
Outcome and governing maintenance authority: Serialize GPU-backed headless initialization within each affected parallel test process in integration, vertical_slice and present_ack, preserving their existing observable lifecycle/render/present-ack assertions. This is authorized T8.0 test-harness maintenance under epic hud-bstmy.1, the residual gap reported by hud-bstmy.1.6/PR #1296, original .1.1/.1.8 serialization outcomes, docs/scope.md T8/Working rules, docs/vision.md (local test signal; cheap idle; work proportional to change), docs/invariants.md, and AGENTS.md's existing test-only serialization contract. The bead authorizes a test-race fix, not a new production scheduling policy. It does not authorize a spec amendment or invariant reduction.

Non-goals: No production mutex inside HeadlessRuntime::new, changed runtime fields/constructor result/error behavior, adapter/backend policy, rendering/frame-loop lock, cross-process/file lock, new Cargo feature/dependency/public API, auth/port/test assertion change, hardware-ICD safety claim, test deletion, unrelated code diet, CI/required-check change or owner decision. Preserve existing runtime-lib full-scenario locks and pixel/compositor helper contracts. Canonical app production_boot and benchmark_config_schema are adjacent constructor surfaces for .1.11's inventory; they are not silently added to this bead.

Evidence-based engineering choice: HeadlessRuntime::new is the public production/artifact-generation constructor (runtime src/headless.rs:200-213); a mutex there would alter every consumer. runtime src/lib.rs:58-59 currently compiles src/test_support.rs only for tests. That source has a pure Tokio async mutex plus lock_headless_runtime and no runtime-crate-specific imports, so it can be included by path once in each external test binary. Reuse that canonical lock source rather than add a production policy or a new helper crate/feature. Add a narrowly named test-only future wrapper, e.g. serialized_headless_init(init), which acquires the existing async gate, awaits the supplied initialization future, and returns its exact output. Every targeted construction caller invokes this wrapper. Keep lock_headless_runtime available for runtime-lib tests that already hold the same gate around an entire scenario; never call the wrapper recursively or from a scenario already holding that gate.

Owned surface and complete current constructor map (re-grep at implementation SHA; line numbers are navigation only):
- crates/tze_hud_runtime/src/test_support.rs owns the canonical test-only gate and wrapper. Production lib.rs cfg(test) boundary stays intact. A path inclusion in each test binary creates one process-local instance; include it exactly once per binary so helper submodules share it rather than creating separate locks.
- tests/integration/common/mod.rs and the four GPU test binaries: multi_agent.rs constructors at 146, 743 and 1060; subtitle_streaming.rs start_runtime_with_subtitle_zone constructor at 106, used by five async tests; text_stream_portal_adapter.rs constructors at 830 and 924; text_stream_portal_cadence.rs constructors at 265, 432 and 729. Add the narrow wrapper through the existing common module where used; adapter/cadence may include the shared lock source or the narrow common GPU module once. Preserve configuration, port allocation, gRPC/MCP setup and all concurrent agent tasks. All other integration files must be searched for raw or indirect GPU construction before declaring the surface complete. poc_acceptance uses the GPU-free HeadlessEventLoopHarness (event_loop_harness.rs:74-80), so it needs no gate merely because it is headless.
- examples/vertical_slice/tests/budget_assertions.rs constructors at 90, 159, 273, 341, 417, 590, 760, 895, 935 and 1012, plus make_scene_runtime at 1118. The helper feeds six explicit scene tests and 13 scene_render_test! expansions at 1344-1408; enumerate those callers, not just the one helper site. The baseline therefore has 29 GPU scenarios here (10 direct tests plus 19 helper-driven scene tests).
- examples/vertical_slice/src/main.rs boot constructor at 80 is shared production code. Its two cfg(test) callers paired_agent_runs_the_full_lifecycle (296) and unpaired_psk_is_rejected (318) must wrap their boot awaits from the test module. Keep production boot/main unchanged. Holding the gate through boot initialization, including its immediate start_grpc_server await, is acceptable; release it before Agent::connect or lifecycle assertions.
- examples/vertical_slice/tests/production_boot.rs:22 is currently one GPU test in its own binary. Record and verify that exception; it cannot have in-process concurrent device creation today. Route through the same test-only helper if doing so simplifies the owned test harness, but do not claim a single-test exception without a complete binary inventory.
- crates/tze_hud_runtime/tests/present_ack.rs make_runtime at 29-37 feeds applied_batch_delivered_as_frame_presented, no_batch_no_ack_and_drain_is_one_shot and multiple_batches_share_one_presented_frame. Include the canonical source once, wrap this constructor, and preserve all batch correlation, one-shot drain and present-wall-clock assertions. Cargo.toml:80-85 requires dev-mode for this target; verification must enable it.
- Existing runtime src/headless.rs test guards and runtime tests/pixel_helpers.rs's initialization mutex remain compatible. Do not convert existing library tests into nested acquisitions; tests that intentionally create two runtimes under one outer guard keep their direct constructors. Compositor common/renderer mutexes are separate test processes and remain unchanged.

Lock lifetime and behavior matrix: The async gate covers the complete HeadlessRuntime::new await or the two test-only boot awaits; one waiter enters at a time across Tokio runtimes/worker threads in that binary. Release it on normal return, Err, panic unwind or cancellation before subsequent client setup, scene mutation, frame rendering, pixel readback, telemetry timing or runtime lifetime. Tokio's mutex does not poison on panic. Do not keep the guard inside HeadlessRuntime or hold it until runtime drop: tests may need multiple live runtimes, and measuring frames under a lifetime lock would serialize unrelated work. Preserve exact Err values and existing panic/skip behavior; failed initialization is not swallowed or retried. Cancellation of a queued waiter must not steal the gate; dropping an in-progress initialization must release it. Never mutate process GPU environment inside parallel Rust tests. This is per-process construction serialization only; separate cargo invocations are not coordinated, and a hardware driver may still hang even with sequential creation. Replay/idempotence is ordinary independent test execution with no persistent serialization state or schema. Rollback is deletion/reversion of test wiring/helper additions; production runtime behavior is unchanged.

Verification and test-growth decision: Existing tests already execute the real GPU constructor/lifecycle/render/present-ack behavior, but no deterministic test currently pins this initialization gate. Add exactly one runtime-lib behavioral regression in src/headless.rs's test module, e.g. headless_initialization_is_serial_and_releases_after_failure, which calls the same new wrapper at the external GPU-initialization boundary. Use controllable async probe futures and explicit polling/oneshot/barrier coordination to show that a second initialization cannot enter until the first leaves, maximum concurrent initialization is one, and another call succeeds after error, panic unwind and cancellation. The regression must fail when the gate is removed; do not test Tokio's mutex in isolation or add source-text assertion tests. It belongs in runtime-lib tests, not in the path-included helper source, so inclusion does not multiply the regression into every binary. Expected net test delta is +1; retain all existing test bodies/assertions except their setup wiring. Site enumeration is manual review evidence, not an additional source-scan test.

Use the actual selected llvmpipe ICD from the current justfile/dry-run (lvp_icd.x86_64.json and Mesa 25 lvp_icd.json are supported; this baseline dry-run selects lvp_icd.json). Bound focused commands and prebuild to separate compilation time from test time; retain the default parallel libtest harness, never --test-threads=1 as proof. Execute the new CPU-only regression, just test-integration, the full vertical_slice test targets including main.rs lifecycle tests and budget_assertions, just production-boot, and cargo test -p tze_hud_runtime --test present_ack --features dev-mode with the same selected ICD/software/required-GPU environment used by the recipes. Run those focused parallel GPU binaries twice to provide the original local-signal proof, recording actual executed test counts and durations. Then run just fmt, just clippy and cargo check --workspace (the integration package must compile), followed by just ci once. Tool-gated skips remain explicit limitations, and a missing adapter/selected ICD is not a successful run. Keep p99 assertions under their existing performance-lane policy; this change does not tighten timing budgets.

Documentation impact: Update AGENTS.md's GPU paragraph to describe the newly covered integration/vertical_slice/present_ack binaries, test-only gate scope, single-test exceptions and per-process limits. Update test_support/common helper comments for path inclusion and construction-only lifetime; amend relevant misleading direct cargo-test examples to use llvmpipe recipe/environment where necessary. Recheck README/CLAUDE/justfile comments for affected claims and change only text made inaccurate by this fix. No docs/invariants.md behavior contract changes or new investigation docs are required. PR evidence must include the complete constructor/macro-caller map, gate lifetime, preserved suite counts, +1 regression delta, commands/results and any environment limitations.
